comment: Changes to /api/v1 since the base release, and to what packages/* export since the parent commit, each accepted on purpose as the exact line scripts/contract-check.mjs prints, with the PR that made it and why installed clients are safe (or BREAKING). CI fails on any other line, and on an openapi line it no longer prints: remove those once a release containing them is the base.

Documents an existing answer: v0.10.1 already answered 409 (ApiError) to a resend of a used invitation or without email; #976 adds the conflict of an invitation whose access has ended. Clients show the error.

New answer: linking a character card a crew row already plays now gives 409 ApiError (code conflict, details.reason character_taken, details.member) instead of a second row, for every client; servers that do so advertise crew-one-row-per-character in /instance/version. An earlier client shows a generic error and the link is not made.
New component, used only by the new POST /api/v1/assets/lookup.
New component, used only by the new POST /api/v1/assets/lookup.

New endpoint (additive): the metadata of many assets in one request, for clients that see the capability asset-lookup in /instance/version. The existing template /api/v1/assets/{assetId} only has GET and the new operation is POST on the fixed path /assets/lookup: the methods differ, and the router gives a static path precedence over a parametric one whatever the order of registration; no existing request changes its answer.
New component LiveSegmentNotReady: the legacy body { code, message } that the live HLS 503 has always sent, now declared on those operations instead of ApiError; the handler is unchanged.
302 with Location to a signed bucket URL, sent as before when signed links are on (S3_PUBLIC_REDIRECT) to browsers without a bearer token; clients with a token keep getting the bytes.
304 without a body on a route that revalidates an ETag: the server has always answered it to If-None-Match with its ETag; only clients that send that header see it, as before.
416 with Content-Range and no body, as the server has always answered a Range it cannot satisfy on the original file; only a client that asks for such a range sees it.

A status the server already sent and the document did not list: the answer, its body (ApiError, or plain text where declared) and when it happens are unchanged; clients already handle it by status and error code.
